what_goes_wrong: Some users have almost no chance of being treated or untreated.
how_to_debug: Propensity distributions, bucket counts, effective sample size, trimming checks.

what_goes_wrong: A feature contains future outcome information or is built after the outcome window.
how_to_debug: Too-good metrics, suspicious feature timing, impossible prediction inputs.

what_goes_wrong: A mediator or downstream variable is used as a confounder.
how_to_debug: Estimated effect changes because part of the treatment pathway is blocked.

what_goes_wrong: Treatment or outcome models are too weak for the adjustment problem.
how_to_debug: Poor nuisance diagnostics, unstable CATE estimates, weak calibration.

what_goes_wrong: Individual treatment effects are treated as precise facts.
how_to_debug: Noisy scatter, unstable deciles, wide bootstrap policy intervals.

what_goes_wrong: Many segments are searched until some look impressive by chance.
how_to_debug: Random segment stress tests and transparent multiple-comparison caveats.

what_goes_wrong: A report gives a point estimate without assumptions, diagnostics, or caveats.
how_to_debug: Checklist requiring estimand, overlap, model diagnostics, sensitivity, and decision context.
